external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third party that settles payments and sends a payment-status webhook.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that serves the storefront, handles shopper sign-in and orders, and receives the payment webhook.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that processes orders and writes order data and receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket receiving a receipt for every completed order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.data_description: Shopper sign-in, browsing, and order data

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable on the worker

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.data_description: Receipt records identifying the order and the order service that wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: Notification that the order is paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

assumptions.assumption: The orders database is confidential because it contains shopper addresses, card-last-four values, and order records.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four live in orders-db.
